gloss: bend, twist, make crooked; do wrong; iniquity, guilt, its punishment; ruin
summary: To bend or twist: a man bowed over in pain, paths made crooked, the face of the earth twisted over, and so to twist what is straight and do wrong. Its noun עָוֺן is the twisted deed, iniquity, named with חַטָּאת and פֶּשַׁע, and scripture follows it through to what it brings: the guilt that is “on” a man and that he “bears”, and the punishment that “finds” him. Yahweh “lifts” iniquity, covers it and forgives it, and his servant bore the iniquity of all. Arabic ʿawā “bend, twist (a rope, a bow); turn aside” shows the bending; the nouns עִי and עַוָּה, a heap of ruins and an overturning, are what is left when a city is twisted down.

words.summary: About 230 times. The same word names the wrong done, the guilt that rests on the doer and is “borne”, and the punishment that comes of it, so that one verse can turn from one to the next (Lam 4:22). It is twisted doing: “they have made their ways crooked (הֶעֱוּוּ)” (Jer 3:21), and its fixed partners are חַטָּאת “sin” and פֶּשַׁע “transgression”.

senses.definition: The wrong a man does, the bending of what is right: named with sin and transgression, confessed, known, remembered, washed, cleansed and forgiven.

evidence.note: “My sin I made known to you, and my עֲוֺנִי I did not cover; I said, I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh.”
“Lifting עָוֺן, transgression and sin”: the three words for wrong together.
“What have I done? What is my עֲוֺנִי, and what is my sin before your father?”
“What is our עֲוֺנֵנוּ, and what is our sin that we have sinned against Yahweh?”
“How many are my עֲוֺנוֹת and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.”
“The law of truth was in his mouth, and wrong (עַוְלָה, of the root עול) was not found on his lips … and many he turned back from עָוֺן”: wrong set against truth and uprightness.
Aaron confesses over the goat “all the עֲוֺנֹת of the sons of Israel and all their transgressions, all their sins”.
“Your עֲוֺנֹתֵיכֶם have separated between you and your God.”
“A people heavy of עָוֺן.”
“Wash me thoroughly from my עֲוֺנִי, and cleanse me from my sin.”
“In עָוֺן I was brought forth, and in sin my mother conceived me.”
“I will cleanse them from all their עֲוֺנָם … and forgive all their עֲוֺנוֹתֵיהֶם.”
“The עֲוֺן of the house of Israel and Judah is very, very great.”
“The עֲוֺן of the Amorite is not yet complete”: wrong that accumulates to a measure.
Those who drag עָוֺן with cords of falsehood, and sin as with cart ropes.
“The עֲוֺן of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.”
Adultery would be “an עָוֺן for judges”, a crime to be judged.

senses.definition: The wrong as it rests on the one who did it and is reckoned to him: guilt that is “on” a man, that he “bears”, that another may take on himself or carry for others, and that Yahweh does not reckon to the forgiven.

evidence.note: “Though he did not know, he is guilty (וְאָשֵׁם) and shall bear his עֲוֺנוֹ.”
“On me, my lord the king, be the עָוֺן, and on my father's house, and the king and his throne be innocent (נָקִי)”: guilt against innocence.
“The man shall be free (וְנִקָּה) from עָוֺן, and that woman shall bear her עֲוֺנָהּ.”
Abigail: “On me, my lord, be the עָוֺן.”
“That person shall be utterly cut off; his עֲוֺנָה is on him.”
“Happy the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon עָוֺן.” Quoted in Rom 4:8.
Psa 32:2 quoted: “blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not reckon sin”.
Shimei: “Let not my lord reckon עָוֺן to me.”
A witness who does not tell “shall bear his עֲוֺנוֹ”.
Aaron, with the plate on his forehead, “shall bear the עֲוֺן of the holy things”.
Aaron and his sons “shall bear the עֲוֺן of the sanctuary”.
The sin offering was given to the priests “to bear the עֲוֺן of the congregation, to make atonement for them”.
“The goat shall bear on itself all their עֲוֺנֹתָם to a land cut off.”
The prophet lies on his side and “bears the עֲוֺן” of Israel and of Judah, a day for a year.
“Yahweh has made to land on him the עֲוֺן of us all.”
“My righteous servant will justify many, and their עֲוֺנֹתָם he will bear.”
“Who himself bore our sins in his own body on the tree”, after Isa 53.
“The son shall not bear the עֲוֺן of the father, nor the father bear the עֲוֺן of the son.”
“Our fathers sinned and are not; we bear their עֲוֺנֹתֵיהֶם.”
“Our עֲוֺנֹתֵינוּ have increased over our head, and our guilt (אַשְׁמָתֵנוּ) has grown up to the heavens.”
“My עֲוֺנֹתַי have gone over my head; like a heavy burden they are too heavy for me.”

senses.definition: What the wrong brings on the doer: the penalty that “finds” him or “meets” him, the destruction a city is swept away in, the punishment a people “accepts” or that is “complete”.

evidence.note: Cain, sentenced to wander (Gen 4:11–12, 14): “my עֲוֺנִי is greater than I can bear”.
Saul to the woman: “As Yahweh lives, no עָוֺן shall meet you for this thing”: the penalty of Lev 20:27.
“If we wait until morning light, עָוֺן will find us.”
“Lest you be swept away in the עֲוֺן of the city”: the destruction that came of it.
“The עֲוֺן of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment.”
“Your עֲוֺנֵךְ is complete, daughter of Zion; he will exile you no more. He will visit your עֲוֺנֵךְ, daughter of Edom”: the punishment ended for one, the wrong punished in the other.
“Her warfare is fulfilled, her עֲוֺנָהּ is accepted (נִרְצָה), for she has received from Yahweh's hand double for all her sins.”
“If their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they accept their עֲוֺנָם.”
“A day for a year you shall bear your עֲוֺנֹתֵיכֶם, forty years.”
The prince of Israel “whose day has come, in the time of the עֲוֺן of the end”.
“Do not be cut off in her עֲוֺנָהּ, for it is the time of Yahweh's vengeance.”
“That wicked man shall die in his עֲוֺנוֹ.”

evidence.locator: Exo.34.7, עָוֺן → ἀνομίας; Psa.32.5; Psa.130.8, עֲוֺנֹתָיו → ἀνομιῶν; Isa.6.7; Isa.27.9; ἀνομία renders עָוֺן ×52

evidence.note: “That he might redeem us from all ἀνομίας”: the words of Psa 130:8, “he will redeem Israel from all his עֲוֺנֹתָיו”.
Jer 31:34 quoted: “their sins and their ἀνομιῶν I will remember no more”.

evidence.locator: Jer.31.34 (LXX 38.34), לַעֲוֺנָם → ταῖς ἀδικίαις; Dan.9.24; ἀδικία renders עָוֺן ×64

evidence.note: “I will be merciful to their ἀδικίαις”: Jer 31:34, “I will forgive their עֲוֺנָם”.

evidence.locator: Psa.32.2, עָוֺן → ἁμαρτίαν; ἁμαρτία renders עָוֺן ×24

evidence.note: Psa 32:2 quoted: “to whom the Lord will not reckon ἁμαρτίαν”.

parallels.note: “Sin”: the commonest partner, often in the same breath.
“Transgression, rebellion”: with עָוֺן and sin in the confession and the forgiving.
“Guilt”: beside עָוֺן as what has grown up to the heavens.

opposites.note: “Innocent, free”: the one on whom no עָוֺן rests.
“Truth”: the law of truth in the mouth, set against the עָוֺן he turned many from.

phrases.gloss: bear iniquity (carry its guilt); lift iniquity (forgive)

evidence.note: The guilty bears his own.
“You shall bear (וְנָשָׂאתָ) the iniquity of the house of Israel.”
Yahweh lifts iniquity: forgives.
“Take away all iniquity (כָּל־תִּשָּׂא עָוֺן).”

phrases.gloss: the time of the punishment of the end

words.gloss: bend, twist, make crooked; do wrong, commit iniquity
words.summary: Seventeen times. The niphal and piel are the bending itself, of a body doubled over in pain and of paths made crooked; the hiphil makes a way or what is right crooked, and with חָטָא and רָשַׁע is the confession “we have done wrong”. The brief's three tokens with no stem (2Ki 18:34; 19:13; Isa 37:13) are the place Ivvah, filed here by spelling.

senses.definition: To act wrongly toward someone or against God.

evidence.note: “Not against the king alone has Vashti the queen עָוְתָה, but against all the princes.”
“We have sinned and עָוִינוּ and done wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments.”

stems.gloss: be bent, bowed; be twisted, perverse

senses.definition: To be doubled over in pain or grief.

evidence.note: “נַעֲוֵיתִי, I am bowed down (שַׁחֹתִי) greatly; all the day I go mourning.”
“Pangs have seized me like a woman in labour; נַעֲוֵיתִי from hearing, I am dismayed from seeing.”

senses.definition: Twisted in mind or way: the perverse, set against the man of insight.

evidence.note: “A man is praised by the mouth of his insight, but נַעֲוֵה לֵב will be for contempt.”
Saul to Jonathan: “son of a נַעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת”, of a perverse, rebellious woman.

senses.definition: To twist a thing out of its straight form: paths made crooked so that one cannot go on, the face of the earth turned over in judgment.

evidence.note: “He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; my paths עִוָּה.”
“Yahweh empties the earth and lays it waste, וְעִוָּה its face, and scatters its inhabitants.”

stems.gloss: make crooked, pervert; do wrong, commit iniquity

senses.definition: To make a way or what is right crooked.

evidence.note: “For הֶעֱוּוּ their way; they have forgotten Yahweh their God.”
“I sinned, and what was upright הֶעֱוֵיתִי, and it was not repaid to me.”

senses.definition: To do wrong, confessed with “we have sinned” and “we have done wickedly”.

evidence.note: “I have sinned, and I הֶעֱוֵיתִי; but these sheep, what have they done?”
“We have sinned וְהֶעֱוִינוּ, we have done wickedly.”
“We have sinned with our fathers; הֶעֱוִינוּ, we have done wickedly.”
Shimei: “what your servant הֶעֱוָה on the day my lord the king went out”.
“They weary themselves הַעֲוֵה”, beside deceit and lies.
Of David's seed: “when he בְּהַעֲוֺתוֹ, I will chasten him with the rod of men”.

words.summary: Five times, plural עִיִּים or עִיִּין but once: what a city becomes when it is thrown down. Its tie to the root is not clear: it may be what is left when a city is overturned (the piel of Isa 24:1, the noun עַוָּה of Ezk 21:32), but no cognate has been found to show it.

senses.definition: The heaps of rubble a destroyed city is turned into.

evidence.note: “Zion shall be ploughed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become עִיִּין, and the mountain of the house high places of a forest.”
Micah's word quoted by the elders of the land.
“I will make Samaria לְעִי of the field … I will pour down her stones into the valley.”
“They have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem לְעִיִּים.”
“Does one not stretch out a hand בְּעִי?”: in the ruin, a man's fall; the line is obscure.

words.summary: One verse, the word three times over: the overturning of the throne of Judah. It is the piel's twisting over (Isa 24:1) made a noun.

senses.definition: A twisting over, a throwing down: of the kingdom and crown taken from the last king of Judah.

evidence.note: After “remove the turban, take off the crown … exalt the low and abase the high” (Ezk 21:31): “עַוָּה עַוָּה עַוָּה I will make it; this also shall be no more, until he comes whose the judgment is, and I will give it.”

words.summary: Once, a plural formed by doubling the root: a spirit of twisting that makes Egypt stagger.

senses.definition: A twisted, reeling state of mind sent on Egypt's counsellors, so that they lead the nation astray like a drunkard staggering.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has mixed within her a spirit of עִוְעִים, and they have made Egypt stagger in all its work, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.”

words.summary: Once, of Damascus, with מַפָּלָה “ruin”: another form of עִי. Its tie to the root is as unclear as that noun's. Not the מֵעִים “bowels” of the root מעה.

senses.definition: A heap, the rubble a city is reduced to.

evidence.note: “Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be מְעִי מַפָּלָה, a heap of ruin.”

cognates.gloss: bend (a thing, a bow); twist (hair, a rope, a turban); turn (a camel's head) by the rein; turn someone from a thing; (form VII) become bent or twisted
cognates.note: The bending and twisting of the niphal and piel, and the turning aside of the hiphil: a straight thing made crooked. Arabic shows ʿ behind ע. The same verb also means “howl” (of a dog or wolf, explained as twisting its muzzle and crying), which has no Hebrew counterpart.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2185, art. عو, عَوَى (n30900)
evidence.note: “He bent a thing … and likewise a bow … he twisted hair, and a rope … عَوَيْتُ رَأْسَ النَّاقَةِ I turned the head of the she-camel by means of the nose-rein … عَوَاهُ عَنِ الشَّىْءِ He turned him from the thing.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2186, art. عو, اِنْعَوَى (n30904)
evidence.note: “It became bent [or twisted].”

cognates.gloss: err, deviate from the right way; (form IV) cause to err, lead astray, seduce
cognates.note: The moral side of the Hebrew, going wrong, deviating from what is right, matches this verb closely, and some set the “do wrong” verb and עָוֺן apart from the bending under a second root with ġ. Scripture itself joins them: the hiphil “they have made their way crooked” (Jer 3:21) and “I perverted what was right” (Job 33:27) are the bending used of conduct, and Lane's own sources gloss the passive of ġawā as being turned aside (لَوَاهُ, “twisted him”). Kept as possible: if it holds, ע here would be ġ and the entry two older roots in one spelling.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2304, art. غو / غوى, غَوَى (n32566)
evidence.note: “He erred; deviated from the right way or course, or from that which was right.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2304, art. غو / غوى, أَغْوَاهُ (n32567)
evidence.note: “He caused him to err … he seduced him, misled him, or led him astray”; غَوَاهُ الهَوَى explained as لَوَاهُ and صَرَفَهُ, “desire turned him aside”.
Compares Arabic غَوَى and أَغْوَى.

cognates.gloss: curve, deviate; (aphel) do wrong; (ithpeel) be wronged
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums holds both sides in one verb: to curve or deviate, and in the aphel to do wrong, used by the Targum of Psa 106:6 for the Hebrew הֶעֱוִינוּ. Aramaic writes ʿ and ġ alike, so it cannot show which stands behind ע.

evidence.locator: s.v. עֲוֵי (ch.), citing Targ. Ps. LIX, 5 (without making a curve, deviation); Targ. Ps. CVI, 6 (Af., to be wrong); Targ. Prov. XVIII, 19 (Ithpe., to be wronged)

evidence.note: Aramaic עויא ʿiwyā, ʿawyā “perversity, sin”.

doctrine.statement: A man who sins “shall bear his iniquity” (Lev 5:1, 17): the guilt rests on him and its end is his death (Num 15:31). Yet scripture also speaks of iniquity borne by another. Aaron bore the iniquity of the holy things, and the priests the iniquity of the sanctuary (Exo 28:38; Num 18:1); the sin offering was given them “to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement” (Lev 10:17); the goat carried all Israel's confessed iniquities away into a land cut off (Lev 16:21–22); Ezekiel lay bound on his side and bore the iniquity of Israel and Judah, a day for a year (Ezk 4:4–6). Isaiah's servant is the end of this: “he was crushed for our iniquities … Yahweh has made to land on him the iniquity of us all … my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities” (Isa 53:5–6, 11). Peter says of Jesus, “who himself bore our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness” (1Pe 2:24); he “was once offered to bear the sins of many, and will appear a second time, without sin, for salvation” (Heb 9:28); God sent his Son “in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, and condemned sin in the flesh” (Rom 8:3); he “was delivered for our offences and raised for our justification” (Rom 4:25). From the verses: to bear iniquity is to carry it and what it brings; the priests, the goat and the prophet showed it in figure, and Jesus, a man of the same flesh as those he saved, bore it to death in his own body and was raised, so that through him the many who believe are justified.

David says, “in iniquity I was brought forth, and in sin my mother conceived me” (Psa 51:7). The wicked man not warned “shall die in his iniquity” (Ezk 3:18), as the father who oppressed “dies in his iniquity” (Ezk 18:18), and in the new covenant “every man shall die for his own iniquity” (Jer 31:30). Ezekiel states the rule: “the נֶפֶשׁ that sins, it shall die; the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father” (Ezk 18:20), while the son who turns from iniquity “shall surely live” (Ezk 18:17). Paul writes, “through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, and so death passed to all men” (Rom 5:12), and “the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Rom 6:23). From the verses: iniquity ends in death, and it is the whole person, the נֶפֶשׁ, that dies; life beyond it is not a possession of man but the gift of God through Christ.

Yahweh proclaimed his name to Moses as one “lifting iniquity, transgression and sin”, who yet “will by no means clear the guilty” (Exo 34:6–7), and Micah asks, “who is a God like you, lifting iniquity … he will tread down our iniquities, and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea” (Mic 7:18–19). David says, “happy the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity” (Psa 32:2), and Paul quotes it of the righteousness reckoned by faith (Rom 4:6–8). In the new covenant Yahweh says, “I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more” (Jer 31:34), quoted of the covenant Christ mediates (Heb 8:12); “he will redeem Israel from all his iniquities” (Psa 130:8) is echoed in Christ, “who gave himself for us, to redeem us from all iniquity” (Tit 2:14). From the verses: forgiveness is Yahweh's own act of lifting iniquity off the one who confesses it, not cancelling his justice; it is promised in the new covenant and given through Christ to those who believe.

To the last king of Judah, “profane, wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come”, Yahweh said, “remove the turban, take off the crown … עַוָּה, עַוָּה, עַוָּה I will make it; this also shall be no more, until he comes whose the judgment is, and I will give it” (Ezk 21:30–32). The sceptre was not to depart from Judah “until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples” (Gen 49:10). Gabriel told Mary of her son, “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever” (Luk 1:32–33), and James applied Amos's words, “I will return and rebuild the tent of David which has fallen” (Act 15:16). From the verses: David's throne was overturned in Zedekiah and has had no king since; it is kept for Jesus, to whom it will be given, and he will reign on it over Israel on the earth.

Micah said, “because of you Zion shall be ploughed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps (עִיִּין), and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest” (Mic 3:12), and a century later the elders recalled it to save Jeremiah (Jer 26:18). Babylon fulfilled it: “they have made Jerusalem heaps” (Psa 79:1). Jesus foretold it again of the rebuilt temple, “there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down” (Mat 24:2), and of the city, “they will dash you to the ground … and will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the time of your visitation” (Luk 19:44); “Jerusalem will be trodden down by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled” (Luk 21:24). From the verses: the heaps Micah foretold came on Jerusalem at Babylon's hand and again in AD 70, both times for the iniquity of its rulers and people, and the city remains under the nations until the times appointed are fulfilled.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key עוה, as the corpus and the brief key it; no existing entry used it, and no existing entry claims עָוֺן as a word (paqad.json only names נָשָׂא עָוֺן as a parallel phrase, and ani.json quotes 1Sa 25:24). BDB keys claimed: p.be.ab עָוֺן; p.bd.aa the verb; p.bd.ad עִי; p.bd.ab עַוָּה; p.bd.ac עִוְעִים; p.bd.ae מְעִי. p.be.ac (BDB's denominative “commit iniquity”) carries exactly the same 20 tokens as p.bd.aa, so only p.bd.aa is named and the bending and the wrongdoing are stems and senses of one verb. Of those 20, the three “no stem” tokens (2Ki 18:34; 19:13; Isa 37:13, וְעִוָּה) are the place Ivvah filed by spelling, so the verb's true count is 17. Left out as places and peoples (no personal names are formed from the root, so no name files): עַוָּה/עִוָּה/עַוָּא Ivvah/Avva (p.be.ad, whose four tokens also include the piel of Isa 24:1 by spelling), the gentilic עַוִּים Avvites/Avvim (p.be.ae; TIPNR Avvim@Deu.2.23 is a group, and its tokens are also counted under p.bf.ad); also the zero-token cross-references p.az.ag, p.bj.ah, p.ci.ad, b.ch.ab, and the places עַי Ai, עִיִּים Iim/Iyim and עֲוִית Avith, which may be formed from עִי “ruin heap” but are not keyed here. Wiktionary's מְעִי “intestine” is מֵעִים of another root (Proto-Semitic *miʕay-), not the Isa 17:1 word. Open questions: (1) One root or two behind ע: Arabic ʿawā “bend, twist” (ʿ) fits the niphal and piel; Arabic ġawā “err, go astray” (ġ) fits the doing wrong and עָוֺן as closely. Scripture's use (Jer 3:21; Job 33:27; Lam 3:9; Pro 12:8) joins twisting and wrongdoing, so ġawā is entered only as possible and ʿawā is named on עָוֺן; a Ge'ez or Ugaritic witness (Dillmann, Leslau, DULAT, not vendored) could settle the sound. (2) The tie of עִי and מְעִי to the root rests only on kin with עַוָּה and the piel of Isa 24:1; no cognate found. (3) Whether Gen 4:13 is “my iniquity” or “my punishment”: filed under punishment from Cain's complaint of the sentence (Gen 4:14). (4) The doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review, especially bearing-iniquity and throne-overturned-until-he-comes. Leads not followed: Payne Smith for any Syriac ʿwy (SEDRA has no such root; Syriac ܥܘܠܐ “iniquity” is root עול, not this); Jastrow's second עֲוֵי (pael “cry”, as Arabic ʿawā “howl”), not entered; CAL for Old and Imperial Aramaic. The Septuagint renders the verb by ἀδικέω and ἀνομέω, which no New Testament verse uses of a passage with this verb, so no Greek is entered for it; Isa 53:5, 6, 11 have no MACULA alignment for עָוֺן.
